summary: An 18,064-to-19,500-seat arena for the Golden State Warriors (NBA) and Golden State Valkyries (WNBA, since 2025), anchoring an 11-acre, privately financed mixed-use development in Mission Bay with 580,000 sq ft of office/lab space (Uber and the Warriors each lease office space in the adjacent towers for their headquarters, per The Real Deal, 2025), 100,000 sq ft of retail (branded "Thrive City" on Chase Center's own site) and a 35,000 sq ft public plaza; designed by MANICA Architecture with Gensler (interiors), built by a Mortenson/Clark Construction joint venture, and opened September 6, 2019.

milestones.text: Golden State Warriors ownership purchases the ~12-acre former Salesforce.com site in Mission Bay
Chase Center opens with a concert by Metallica and the San Francisco Symphony; the Warriors first play there on October 5, 2019 (preseason)
Chase Center achieves LEED Gold certification (Building Design and Construction: New Construction), one of few major US sports venues to do so
The Real Deal reports that Uber and the Golden State Warriors each lease office space in the adjacent Mission Bay 3 & 4 towers (1655 & 1725 3rd St) for their headquarters

SF Board of Supervisors approves a separate, Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex (129-room hotel, 21 condos, ~25,000 sf retail) next to Chase Center at the northeast corner of the arena (Bisnow, July 2020); the article says the Warriors had not said when they hope to start construction, and no later status was found. Its relationship to this parcel (8722025) is not confirmed -- see open questions. Not treated as this record's own status: Chase Center itself opened in 2019 and remains complete regardless of this separate, unconfirmed proposal.

The Golden State Valkyries (WNBA expansion team) make their WNBA debut on May 16, 2025 (Wikipedia); the SF Chronicle reported in December 2024 that the first regular-season game was scheduled for Chase Center against the Los Angeles Sparks

California Superior Court upholds the subsequent Environmental Impact Report certified by OCII for the Warriors Arena Project, in litigation filed by the Mission Bay Alliance against OCII, the City and others

OCII Commission adopts Resolution No. 14-2026, approving a Sixth Amendment to the Mission Bay South Signage Master Plan that increases character heights and awning-sign flexibility for mixed-use retail and for the Event Center Sign Program at the Warriors event center on Blocks 29-32 (adopted 4-0 with one absence)

open_questions: 2026-09-23: this record's map shape was moved off its Assessor parcel record (the record was previously keyed to block/lot 8722025) because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Uber Mission Bay 3 & 4 towers byte-identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The new geometry is the full Assessor parcel with both Uber towers' own real OSM building footprints subtracted out; how it was built is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record). Two small structures inside the resulting polygon are not yet identified: an oval building in the west plaza, and possibly others not yet checked against satellite imagery.

Chase Center's cost: $1.4B is the most-repeated figure (Construction Dive's headline and Wikipedia's infobox). A $1.3B alternate figure attributed to a Warriors executive had no support in its cited source and was removed on 2026-09-29. A separate 2019 Construction Dive piece on the (distinct, unbuilt) hotel/condo proposal used '$1.5B Chase Center' in its own headline, which appears to conflate the arena with that proposal; that figure is not used here.

Uber's and the Warriors' current lease status was not independently verified beyond The Real Deal's February 2025 report; an earlier '20-year lease', '~4,000 employees' and '145 parking spaces' claim was removed on 2026-09-29 because no readable source states it.

The Warriors-proposed hotel/condo/retail complex on adjacent Blocks 29-30 is financially and physically tied to Chase Center but may sit on a separate parcel; whether it falls within blklot 8722025 or is a distinct, not-yet-built record is not confirmed. Current 2026 construction status is also unconfirmed.

No primary Port of San Francisco or OCII page dedicated specifically to Chase Center was found (as a privately financed project, it may not have one); the only agency-level source found was SFPUC/CleanPowerSF's sustainability write-up.
No openly licensed image was found; recommend linking rather than hosting until one is confirmed.
No opening date found for The Sarap Shop (1 Warriors Way): checked its own Thrive City vendor page for a firm date; retail_confirmed.csv's own opened field is also blank.

As of 2026-09-29: the first photo (exterior, taken 2019-07-27) shows the arena under construction, before the 2019-09-06 opening milestone, so it fits none of the image categories used here; it keeps the 'now' category pending a decision. The interior photo (2019-12-27) was re-tagged 'completed' (within a year after opening). Chase Center's Thrive City tenant list was read on its live page on 2026-09-29 ('Open Now'); tenants not on it (Siren, b8ta, Mission Bay Wine Bar) have not been re-confirmed open.
